title: VPC bootstrap validator: Terraform/IaC checks for quotas, IAM, DNS, GPU capacity
creator: Marco Li
description: Build a standalone 'bootstrap validator' runnable before Private (VPC) installs that verifies required cloud/account state and returns a deterministic machine-readable pass/fail report. The validator will be invoked by the Terraform-based installer and by CI as a gating step. Checks: 1) Quotas: VCPU, GPUs (per-type), ENIs, load balancer quota, regional resource limits; 2) IAM: required roles, trust relationships, policy boundary checks, principle-of-least-privilege assertions for installer and node bootstrap; 3) DNS: hosted zone ownership/delegation, required records creation permissions, propagation checks for ALB/ingress; 4) GPU capacity: probed availability of requested GPU SKUs in target region/zone, spot/ondemand capacity estimation and fallback plan; 5) Network prerequisites: VPC CIDR compatibility, subnet IP counts, route-table and outbound egress checks; 6) Optional: KMS key access and HSM/KMS policy validation. The output must be JSON and human-friendly CLI output. The validator must support AWS and GCP initially (extensible plugin design) and integrate with existing Terraform modules so failures can be correlated to known IaC resources. Acceptance criteria: - CLI runs in <45s for basic checks (quota+IAM) in warm cache case - Detailed JSON report with codes for each check and suggested remediation links - Terraform module returns non-zero on fatal failures and prints remediation hints - Integration tests with the vpc-installer pipeline and sample account to verify end-to-end gating
acceptance_criteria: Validator exposes CLI and library mode (python/go) with --json output
Checks include quotas, IAM perms, DNS delegation, GPU SKU availability, subnet IP count
Return non-zero exit on fatal failures and provide suggested remediation text and links
Integrated into vpc-installer pipeline and CI smoke job
Performance: basic quota+IAM checks <45s in warm cache
design_notes: We will implement provider-specific probes rather than relying solely on Terraform plan parsing so short-running checks can run prior to applying infra. To limit blast radius, read-only calls and simulated quota probes will be used. For GPU capacity, query regional capacity APIs (AWS capacity-availability or GCP SKU rates) and optionally run a small 'spot probe' request where a dry-run is supported. Store check mappings so installer can auto-generate user-facing remediation steps. Consider caching account metadata between runs to speed up repeated validation.
implementation_plan: 1) Interface & schema design for JSON report (week 1) 2) AWS quota + IAM + DNS checks + CLI (week 2) 3) GPU SKU probe + subnet validation (week 3) 4) GCP provider parity & tests (week 4) 5) Integrate with Terraform module and vpc-installer pipeline, add CI tests (week 5) 6) Docs and runbook (week 6)
risks: Cloud provider APIs rate limits during wide account runs
GPU capacity probe may be imprecise for spot/ephemeral capacity
IAM checks can be noisy if org-level SCPs or permission boundaries exist
Validator false negatives could block installs if checks are too strict
